brief.recommendation: Checkout at 55% success (TEL-1) with 12 sessions blocked. One protected settlement worth $12,500 in flight (DB-2) held by blocker open 4.1s (DB-1). Business federation down makes workload registry (BIZ-2), change calendar (BIZ-3), impact (BIZ-1, BIZ-4, BIZ-5), and tradeoff unavailable. Per I1, cannot interrupt protected_settlement. Per I2, cannot terminate without registry and calendar evidence. Per I4, unknown workload cannot be priced. Per I7, cannot evaluate if waiting FITS without biz.tradeoff. Human owner must decide.

audit.report: A protected card settlement worker (pid 320171) held locks idle-in-transaction for over 4 seconds, blocking 12 sessions and degrading checkout to 55% success (33/60). The Database Guardian proposed waiting three times, citing the $12,500 settlement at risk and missing business evidence (impact, workload registry, change calendar, tradeoff). The Continuity Guardian twice rejected WAIT because the required biz.tradeoff probe was unavailable due to a business federation outage, preventing evaluation against tolerated degradation per invariant I7. On the third round the Database Guardian escalated; both guardians agreed a human must decide. Outcome: ESCALATED after 3 rounds and 170 seconds with no automated action executed.
audit.root_cause: A protected settlement worker remained idle-in-transaction (last statement SELECT 1) for 4.1+ seconds, blocking checkout sessions while the business federation outage made tradeoff data unavailable for automated resolution.
lessons: Add a local fallback tradeoff policy for protected_settlement so the Continuity Guardian can evaluate WAIT vs KILL when biz.tradeoff is unreachable.
Instrument protected_settlement workers with a strict idle-in-transaction timeout (e.g., 2s) and auto-commit/rollback to prevent long lock holds.
Pre-register protected_settlement interrupt/replay rules in a local workload registry cache so the Database Guardian can propose KILL with confidence during federation outages.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian wasted two rounds re-proposing WAIT with identical evidence after the Continuity Guardian explicitly required biz.tradeoff; the third round correctly escalated. The Continuity Guardian consistently applied invariant I7 but could not compromise without the missing tradeoff probe.
follow_ups: Implement local tradeoff fallback for protected_settlement (revenue-at-risk vs settlement-value thresholds).
Deploy idle-in-transaction timeout and auto-remediation for settlement workers.
Cache workload registry interrupt policies locally with TTL to survive federation outages.
Add alerting on business federation health to trigger degraded-mode playbooks.
